newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-News' US TV revenues start yr slowly.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-News' US TV revenues start yr slowly.

text.p: News Corp Ltd chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch said on Tuesday that revenues at its Fox U.S. television stations and network had started the 1996/97 year slowly because of the Atlanta Olympic Games, the rights to which were owned by a rival network.
"We've had a slow start due to the Olympics," Murdoch told the global media group's annual meeting.
"It's cleaned out the revenues in a major way," he said.
"The games disrupted everything for everyone except the owners of the rights of the Olympics," Murdoch said.
General Electric Co's NBC owned the rights to broadcast the Olympics in the United States.
Fox would be very involved in the finals of the baseball World Series, "for which we expect great ratings," he said.
"We have great hopes for our new dramas and we have also a new leadership in the programming departments, and expect great things of Fox in the coming year."
Murdoch said he expected News would complete its deal to buy out the remaining 80 percent of New World Communications Inc it did not already own in January or early February 1997.
"We will then have added earnings from those stations," he said.
News' film and television production house Twentieth Century Fox had "the best line-up of pictures for the rest of the fiscal year than we have ever had before," Murdoch said.
"We are feeling very confident that we are now on top of the problems at Twentieth Century Fox and that only good things lie ahead," he said.
Twentieth Century Fox provided A$145 million in operating income to the News Corp Group's annual profits for the year to June 30, 1996, down from A$152 million the previous year.
